text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Interest rates will be kept at the present level in the near future, National Bank president Gyorgy Suranyi said on Friday, adding he foresees 3 percent GDP growth in 1997 and 17 percent inflation by the end of the year. (Sat.)

- The Agricultural Producers' Advocacy Organisation decided Saturday to call on members and supporters to stage go-slow demonstrations on Wednesday on roads leading to the major border crossings and the capital.
- Parliament is expected on Tuesday to amend the tax and social insurance regulations affecting farmers, deputy Speaker Agnes Maczo Nagy announced on Friday. (Sat.)

- The Socialist Party congress set for June 6-7 will discuss the current political situation, determine tasks for the near future, and elect a new financial supervisor, but will not deal with any other personnel issues.

- Democratic People's Party president Ivan Szabo said his party seeks to normalise relations with the Democratic Forum (from which they split one year ago), and noted they would be pleased to see the Young Democrats mediate between the two parties.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Intelligence Office last fall collected data on contacts of several MPs, most of them Socialists, without informing Istvan Nikolits, minister in charge of the civil secret services.
- After two years of decline, the real wages of public sector workers show a 4-5 percent increase for the first quarter of 1997 compared to the same period last year.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn Friday received Anita Gradin, the EU commissioner for justice and interior affairs. (Sat.)
- The Chief Prosecutor's Office filed charges in the Metropolitan Court Friday against Albert Szabo for the crime of incitement against the Jewish people. (Sat.)

- A confidential document sent by the British consultancy ETD Kft., based in Budapest, to Britain's industry minister expresses apprehension over the slowing down of the privatisation of Hungarian energy. The letter was also sent to Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Net household savings came to HUF 40.9 billion last month, according to the National Bank.

- The Swedish company Saab AG has worked out a proposal for the Hungarian government on financing the latter party's purchase of fourth-generation Gripen fighter planes, managing director Bengt Halse announced on Friday at the opening of Saab's Budapest office.
- The equity of the broadcasting company Antenna Hungaria was increased by HUF 2.5 billion to HUF 10.35 billion by the State Privatisation and Holding Co.
- The brewery Borsodi Sorgyar closed last year with a pre-tax profit of HUF 1.6 billion, managing director Gyula Bogdan announced.
- Magyar Cetelem Bank Rt. will shortly receive its license of operation, said managing director Janos Lendvay.
- A new travel insurance firm owned by Generali Budapest and Providencia opened its doors on Friday. (Sat.)
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The president of Magyar Aluminum Rt. has asked the minister of industry and trade and the head of the Hungarian Energy Office to reduce energy prices for large-scale corporate consumers.
